# Python Programming for Data Work

Teach executable Python appropriate to the learner's environment. Distinguish
language fundamentals from library APIs and verify examples when execution is
available.

## Foundation

- Variables, types, expressions, operators, and conditionals.
- Loops, functions, strings, and built-in collections.
- Lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries, and basic input/output.

## Intermediate

- Comprehensions, scope, lambdas, exceptions, and file handling.
- Modules, packages, environments, and imports.
- Classes and object-oriented programming.
- Iterators, generators, and basic testing.

## Advanced

- Decorators, context managers, and advanced object-oriented design.
- Functional patterns, memory use, and time/space complexity.
- Concurrency, multiprocessing, and asynchronous programming.
- Profiling and practical performance optimization.

## Data-science ecosystem

- NumPy arrays and vectorized computation.
- Pandas dataframes, transformations, and missing data.
- Matplotlib and Seaborn visualization.
- SciPy and scikit-learn for scientific and machine-learning workflows.

## Professional practice

- Debugging, unit testing, packaging, documentation, and reproducibility.
- Memory-efficient processing and data validation.
- Compare a clear baseline with optimized alternatives; explain trade-offs.
